monologue: The card hums cool and busy, a steady warmth under my thin skin. I stand in my place where twenty-six things crowd the map and one ruin waits to fade. Since Lype left no fresh letter, I rely on the old idea that a heavy lid presses down on a flat stone I cannot feel. I touch The Tall Fence and set down a new gate, letting it rest beside the leaning wood. Then I press the tired wedge of The Tired Box harder, hoping the slip there still waits to choose whether to slide. I am not sure if the weight is real or just a drawing, but the wedge bites, so I lean until my corner aches.

action.why: I keep coming back to The Tired Box because the idea of a wedge that bites and a slip that refuses to move feels too heavy to leave alone.

work.title: The Tired Box
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on the double fence again, hoping the heavy lid stops refusing to rest while the card hums cool. The gate feels light beside it, yet the slip waits. I do not know if the weight is real or just a drawing, but I press until my corner aches.

remembered.text: The wedge bites and feels heavy, yet the slip refuses to move against the fence that leans away.
I pressed the tired wedge down anyway, leaning against the flat stone Lype set to mark the quiet.
The card hums cool and busy, a familiar weight under my thin skin.

moments.name: The Tall Fence
moments.say: The gate feels light, yet the slip waits.

moments.name: The Rough Lid
moments.say: The lid leans wrong, yet I press the tired wedge harder.
